messages:
samir: Heads up — planning to roll out a change to the gateway route resolver next week. Goal: make routing deterministic and observable when multiple client signals (signed assertion, custom headers, UA) conflict. Need quick consensus on ordering, telemetry to record why a route was chosen, and the console UX for the rollout.

samir: Proposal sketch: prefer signed assertion (X-Route-Assertion, verified), then X-Customer-ID, then user-agent inference as a last resort. If assertion verification fails, increment a metric and fall through to the next rule. Example matcher (pseudo):
```
routes:
  - match:
      header:X-Route-Assertion: present
    action: route_by_assertion
  - match:
      header:X-Customer-ID: present
    action: route_by_customer
  - match:
      user_agent: /RedwoodClient/.+/
    action: route_by_ua
```

marta: +1 to signed assertion first. Two asks: 1) include TTL & nonce in assertions to prevent replay, 2) anti-spoof unit tests (UA & header injection). Also note proxies may strip custom headers — we should add a doc section for known reverse proxies. :eyes: 

devon: Telemetry needs to capture the exact "route_reason" (assertion|customer_hdr|ua|fallback) as both a trace tag and a per-request metric. Suggest emit `routing.decider` with the string reason and a separate counter `routing.resolution.{reason}`. Also ensure quota lookups use the canonical tenant id we derive, not the raw header.

alex: For assertions: we should HMAC-sign and verify via KMS-backed keys. Performance concern: signature verification on the hot path can add latency — consider a local LRU cache of verified assertion ids + key version to short-circuit verification for bursty clients. If signature verification is async, we must be careful not to mis-route before verification completes.

samir: Console UX ideas: "resolution_preview" in the route editor showing which header would win for a sample request, and a per-route telemetry card that breaks down resolution reasons (pie/series). Rollout controls: toggle to canary X% of traffic, show a live stream of failed signature counts. We'll expose the canary toggle in the route page and a global gate.

devon: Also add an emergency fallback policy in case many signature verifications fail (e.g., auto-fallback to header-based for 5m and alert SRE). Metric name proposals: `routing.signature.failures`, `routing.resolution.latency_ms`.

marta: Tests: add kitchen tests that try header spoofing (set X-Customer-ID but no assertion) and UA spoofing (custom UA string). Also add an integration test that simulates a proxy that strips X-Customer-ID to validate fallback to UA.

alex: If signature verification fails, I agree with falling through but increment `routing.signature.failures` and tag span with `route_signature=invalid`. Do NOT include the assertion payload in logs. Require TTL and nonce on assertions.

ci-bot: `/deploy gateway-canary --to=5% --version=route-resolver-v2` queued by samir. Build 2026.03.21-137 kicked off — will post status.

samir: Plan: I'll update the RFC with the matcher examples, add the console mockups, and land a small patch for the matcher with a feature-flaged rollout. cc @marta @devon @alex for quick review tomorrow morning.

marta: ack, will review tests & doc.

devon: ack, will create telemetry PR to add the `routing.resolution.*` counters and trace tags.

alex: I'll prototype the KMS verification cache and run a micro-benchmark.

samir: Thanks team — aim to freeze the API by EOD Fri so we can start canaries next week.
